original_card.question: Can one specified masked or overcomplete decoder improve the complete moment budget?
methods: Synthesize a decoder with exact coefficients and fully priced helper endpoints.
Bound the best possible budget for a fixed support alphabet before synthesis.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound and count all copied information, frames and restoration.

first_step.inspect: Locate the excluded classes: masked identities, at least nine terms, and deeper punctures.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one finite support alphabet and test exact decoding constraints before building a whole network.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A cheaper fully realized decoder could increase deficit or lower recursive cost on the binding complex side.
allowed_variations: Select a specific masked or overcomplete family with exact labels and supports.
scope_change_triggers: Repeating the exact eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: On the pinned P112 coordinate matrix, can a real ten-term factorization that keeps the eight coordinate readers and adds two totals lower the pairing-rank sum below 64 when the correction sources are supported on at most three ports?
scope_change_reason: The card allows one specified overcomplete family on a fixed support alphabet. This family is the real two-total extension of the eight coordinate readers, which p112-single-lift leaves open, cut at the sharp full-row absorption scale of three ports. It does not repeat the eight-term all-pairs search. Frames and restoration are not given a separate positive price because this copy-rank relaxation already stays at least 64.
bottleneck_link: The complex side binds. A ten-term decoder that lowered the P112 coordinate copied-information charge could increase the complex deficit. This note shows that charge does not fall for real corrections supported on at most three ports, including every real full-row absorption. It is a scoped obstruction, not a new supplier.
stop_rule: Stop once the plane census, the eight-reader cocircuit census, and the support-size corollary are certified, including the sharp three-row invoice and the failure controls. Do not search supports of size 4 or larger.
evidence: All 6216 row pairs are independent and form exactly 896 three-point planes, with no four coplanar rows. Each of the eight readers has the same 255-form split histogram, and every rank-dropping deletion has size at least 24. The zero correction costs 64. The sharp three-port absorption costs 68. The predecessor rank and an independent column-wise rank agree. Controls reject a 23-port drop, a missed dependence, and a mutated Gram row.
author: Riquelme Soares (@hevlyo)
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance was used for the argument, the checkers, and the write-up.

open_questions.question: Can a real rank-2 correction supported on at least 24 ports make this same ten-term pairing-rank sum strictly less than 64?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Twenty-four is the first size at which a coordinate reader can lose pairing rank. A sum below 64 would be copy-rank headroom in the fixed-reader two-total family; a matching lower bound would extend the one-total theorem.
open_questions.first_step: Fix one explicit 24-port positive form on reader 0, cancel a second reader on a subset of that form, solve for (z, w), and recompute all ten pairing ranks with both rank implementations in this package.
open_questions.blocked_by: Cancelling three or more readers at one port overdetermines (z, w), and the shared extra terms are not bounded by the per-reader (7, 7) split. PR 2382 excludes a neighboring model through 47 ports, but that proof is not on this checkout and uses a different cancellation shape.
